newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia moves to cancel Timor human rights meeting.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia moves to cancel Timor human rights meeting.

text.p: Malaysia will not allow local human rights groups to hold a conference on East Timor for fear of harming its ties with Indonesia, the national Bernama news agency quoted a junior minister as saying on Monday.
The Malaysian Cabinet has decided not to allow the Second Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor, organised by non-governmental organisations (NGOs), Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said.

"The government does not try to restrict any activity which brings a positive effect. But this activity will place Malaysia in a spot, especially in relation to its friendship with Indonesia," Megat Junid was quoted as telling a news conference after advising the NGOs to cancel the conference.
Conference organisers, however, told Reuters they could not immediately decide whether to heed Megat Junid's call.

"We haven't made a decision yet. Our position is that we are in principle committed to this conference, which is a private meeting, and see no legal reason for the government to stop it," Sharaad Kuttan, an official of the organising committee, told Reuters.
Kuttan said a decision was expected by Tuesday.
The three-day conference is scheduled to be held in Kuala Lumpur from November 9.
It basically aims to condemn Jakarta's annexation of East Timor in 1975, and alleged violation of human rights in the area by Indonesian authorities.
A similar conference was held in Manila in 1994, despite protests by the Indonesian government.
Malaysia has often resorted to a clear policy of not interfering in the domestic politics of its neighbours, especially members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
